newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down two at 962 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down two at 962 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 962 as of July 18, down two from the prior week and 172 above the year-ago total of 790, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by nine to 807, while rigs working offshore rose five to 129. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose two to 26.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down by 19, California, which was down by seven and Wyoming, which was up by six.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count was up by five at 125.
A total of 381 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 13 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 15 to 578, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at three.
There were 222 rigs drilling directionally, 71 drilling horizontally and 669 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by eight to 384, versus 298 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
